newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Battered dlr struggles, Euro shares wallow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Battered dlr struggles, Euro shares wallow.

text.p: The dollar struggled in European trade on Thursday after tumbling by more than two yen overnight, while Europe's key bourses fell after a disappointing close on Wall Street.
The U.S. currency fell to around 115.60 yen in Asia, its lowest level against the yen since January, and fell further in European trade touching a low of around 114.70 yen before rallying.
Top-level Japanese officials jumped in to try and stem the dollar's freefall, saying the Group of Seven agreement reached in April had filtered through to the markets "sufficiently".
Such comments -- made by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the finance ministry's international finance bureau -- had an effect, pulling the dollar off its lows.
But then comments by a leading Japanese politician sparked fresh speculation about higher Japanese interest rates.
The dollar's fall against they yen also dragged it dollar down against the mark, and although the market soon recovered from the initial shock, traders said the U.S. currency looked far from healthy.
"When dollar/yen fell on the interest rate remarks it triggered long-term stops all over the place, in dollar/mark as well," said one trader at a U.S. bank here.

Koichi Kato, secretary-general of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party, was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying Japan may face pressure to change its current low interest rates as it progresses with financial market deregulation.
Kato's remark drove dollar down to 114.70 yen, its lowest since December 26, though it had rallied to around 115.50 1100 gmt.
Dollar/mark softened in tandem, standing at 1.6885 against Wednesday's close of 1.6965.
Analysts said that judging from dollar/yen's slight rebound, the market realised it had overreacted to Kato's comment.

"There is a view in the market that we're going to get a rate hike in Japan, although I think that's premature," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International here. "So the market is very sensitive to that kind of comment right now, as it's not absolutely convinced it (a rate hike) is going to happen," Richardson said.
However, the dollar's rebound was small compared to its overnight plunge and the market was still nervous, particularly ahead of a slew of U.S. data due later in the day.

April consumer prices at 1230 GMT would be the highlight, as a bigger-than-expected drop in producer prices on Wednesday shocked the market and further clouded prospects of a rate hike at the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.

Behind the dollar's tumble overnight was speculation the U.S. would support a stronger yen, fuelled by talk a newsletter from a Washington-based consulting firm stated Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was calling for a dollar/yen rate of 115. Subscribers to the newsletter denied receiving such a report.

Elsewhere, Europe's leading share markets were all showing early losses. Investors were disappointed that Wall Street only ended 12 points higher having been some 52 points higher at the close of European trade on Wednesday.
In London, the FTSE 100 slid on profit-taking at the start and was down 25.8 points, or 0.5 percent, at 4,661.1 at 1100 gmt. The market, Europe's biggest, has stormed higher in recent days.
"The market has had huge momentum and is at its most technically overbought since 1989 and technically and fundamentally it is due some kind of consolidation," said BZW strategist, Steve Wright.
French stocks opened lower as investors took profits on the bourse's rally to record highs on Wednesday.
Traders said investors were feeling cautious ahead of the U.S. consumer price index.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.35 points at 2,770.28, having picked itself off its opening lows.

Fresh polls showing the conservatives likely to win a majority of seats in the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election had little impact on the bourse. Traders say the market is unlikely to show much reaction unless polls signal a sharp change in sentiment.
German shares were also down in early listless trade as dealers said the market was searching for fuel for a new advance on record levels.
STOCK PRICES AT 1100 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 25.8 points at 4,661.1.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 4.35 points at 2,770.28.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 13.27 points at 3,560.42.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6885 marks in late trade compared with 1.6977 on Wednesday and 115.50 yen versus 118.83.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed at $348.10 after closing at $348.65 an ounce in London on Wednesday. Traders said pressure came from a newspaper report that Germany wanted to sell Bundesbank reserve gold. But solid support was seen at $347.
